chapter: Instruments, first jobs and the regional scene
title: Albert System versus Boehm clarinet
summary: Joe describes his first ebonite clarinet, the Conn Albert System his father ordered, and why he thinks the Albert has better tone.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Let me ask you about the actual instruments you were playing at that time. What system were you playing?
It was an Albert System. My first clarinet was an old clarinet that was a hard rubber piece; they made them out of ebonite, they called it.
In those days?
That's right.
I thought ebonite came after...
It was something they called... Something that broke real easy, I know that. I'm pretty sure they

called it ebonite. Anyway, I cracked the thing. There was no way to fix it. So my Dad said, "I see you like to play the clarinet." So he gets this Sears Roebuck catalogue, picks out a Conn clarinet for twenty-eight dollars, brand-new, beautiful little case -- but it was an Albert System. And the thing about it is, Manuel Roque played a Boehm System -- in those days.
That was the first Boehm Systems, before they had so many keys?
Yeah. But still it was a Boehm.
I mean, I'm not a clarinet player, so naturally I'm not that much up on the technical thing. But why did they make Boehm System clarinets? Was it just easier to play or what?

Yes. After you learned the system, for the simple reason that they had more notes, where you can... Some notes, you have four different ways to make them on the Boehm, and you've only got one or two ways to make on an Albert, you see.
You started playing Albert.
Right.
And then in later years you switched to Boehm.
I switched.
Darensbourg - 36
Well, later on we'll get to where you switched and why. But was... I'll just ask you this directly. Is there any difference in the tone, in your opinion, from the two of them?
Yes.
What is it?
I think an Albert has got a much better tone.
Every clarinet player I've ever talked to or interviewed, including George, Barney, several of them, they all say the same thing.
True.
Then you might say you'd sacrifice a little bit of tone to get to the easier...

Well, for the technique. But I don't know... If you studied the Albert System enough, and really got the rudiments of it and really... What greater technicians can you find than the great old clarinet masters out of Italy and France and places. All they played was an Albert System.
Why do you think the tone was better on an Albert?
